title: São Nicolau in the Cape Verde islands becomes a settlement of the crown: 1,700 Andalusī settlers

The first test of the new reign. The Emperor Muḥammad, wanting to finish his father's work and prove himself a worthy heir, orders the army north for a swift conquest of Castile. The princes Ismāʿīl and Aḥmad talk him round: Galicia would be the nobler and harder conquest, and Navarre after it, for the Basques are a far more redoubtable people than the Castilians. For now the Emperor is convinced

data.context: Castile is allied to the Angevin Empire and Navarre; Galicia has no allies (world file of 2 July 1429)

title: Al-Andalus declares war on Galicia, the greatest of the successor states of Castile: the fifth war of the Istirdād, the War of Shant Yāqub

data.target: Galicia, King Diego Villamarín (31 towns in July 1429)
data.attackers: al-Andalus and all seven ṭāʾifas; the Mamlūks, Morocco and Tunis called (potential)
data.forces: al-Andalus 4,619 regulars and 50 ships; Galicia no men under arms, 2 ships

title: The war plan is as plain as the Emperor's demand: take the capital. The armies march north on Santiago

data.account: There is now careful plan to the Emperor's demand. Take the capital. So the armies march north (Trent)

title: Before Santiago de Compostela the Emperor's nephew Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī, seventeen, with 4,900 men, breaks 7,000 Galicians, killing or taking 3,800 for the loss of 230

commanders.al-Andalus: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad, the Emperor's nephew (56/60/37)

title: The Emperor Muḥammad is now counted worldly: the years he spent with the fleets, in harbours and among fishermen and travellers, have taught him how things get done. His eyes are still on the sea

data.trait: Worldly: practical experience gathered firsthand in workshops, harbours and counting-houses has taught our ruler how to get things done; military tactics +0.05 (the game's text)
data.account: his grandfather put him in charge of the Empire's navies from a young age; that respect for fishermen, harbours and those who travel has not left him, as his eyes remain locked on the sea (Trent)

title: Prince Aḥmad of the dīwān is now counted an architect. He takes after his forebears, a builder imagining the greatest structures for the capital

data.trait: Architect: buildings construction efficiency +10%; from the smallest hut to the loftiest halls, no building is too insignificant to spark this individual's architectural curiosity (the game's text)
data.account: Aḥmad takes after his forebearers. A builder, imagining the greatest structures for the capital (Trent)

title: One of the most purposeful things the late Emperors did was to surround Muḥammad with able counsel. His three wives, Magdalena, Isabel and Jadīla, were chosen for their blood but also for their minds, and with his two eldest sons they carry great weight at court while the Emperor's eyes wander to his own projects

Santiago de Compostela falls after a siege of fifteen days, its garrison broken by hunger and disease and allowed to march out. On the Emperor's direct orders the Cathedral of Santiago, the shrine of the Apostle and the end of the pilgrim road of all Christendom, is destroyed; its Pórtico de la Gloria is carried off to Ishbīliya. The consequences remain to be seen

data.siege: 15 days; the garrison succumbed to hunger and disease and was allowed to march out (the game's text)
data.destroyed: Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela, a work of art (monument, masterpiece 85%), begun in 1075 under Alfonso VI; 'the culmination of the Camino de Santiago, the most travelled Christian pilgrimage route of the medieval world, believed to enshrine the tomb of the Apostle James the Great' (the game's text)
data.captured: the Pórtico de la Gloria, taken to Ishbīliya
data.orders: destroyed on the direct orders of the Emperor (Trent)
data.history: al-Manṣūr took Santiago in 997 and carried its bells to Córdoba, but left the tomb

title: At Oviedo the last army of Galicia, 3,229 men, attacks the host of the Ṭāʾifa of Liyūn, 5,602 under Juan Cangas, and is destroyed to the last man without loss to the defenders
source: save of 17 August 1430 (the war's battle list)

title: The peace with Galicia is not so simple. Its annexation is beyond question, but the two princes are not done in the north: their father is set on destroying the Castilians, and the realm is not ready for a war with the Angevins. Then an opening: Navarre has allied itself to Castile, and while Castile is under London's protection, Navarre is not. If the armies already in the north overwhelm both before London decides whether it must help, the crown has its chance
Al-Andalus declares war on Navarre, the sixth war of the Istirdād. Castile alone answers Navarre's call; the Angevin Empire stays out

data.forces: al-Andalus 4,674 men under arms; Navarre and Castile none, 9 ships between them
data.angevins: allied to Castile, not in the war

title: Before Bilbao the army of al-Andalus, 4,673 strong, breaks 3,580 Navarrese, killing or taking 2,756 for the loss of 191
By 3 November the Castilians have been swept aside by the advance and the armies of al-Andalus are at the gates of Bilbao. All three states, Galicia, Navarre and Castile, fall
The Peace of Ṣafar with Galicia: at 82 war score the kingdom is annexed whole, its 31 towns from Santiago and A Coruña to Oviedo and Llanes. King Diego Villamarín goes into exile at Augsburg

data.exile: Diego Villamarín appears in the save of 3 November as a man of the burghers' estate of Augsburg

title: The Peace of Ṣafar with Navarre and Castile: at 59 war score both are annexed, Navarre's ten Basque towns from Bilbao and San Sebastián to Vitoria and Castile's last four on the Cantabrian coast, Santander, Laredo, Potes and San Vicente. The Kingdom of Castile is no more

data.angevins: the Angevin Empire, Castile's ally, never entered the war
data.kings: Fernando of Castile and his heir Juan are afterwards of the court of the Ṭāʾifa of Burghush, Alfonso Gastón of Navarre of the Ṭāʾifa of Banbalūna

title: Iberia is conquered. With Galicia, Navarre and Castile gone, every town of the peninsula belongs to the Emperor or to one of his ṭāʾifas: the Istirdād is complete

The conquered north is shared among the ṭāʾifas of the frontier: the eight towns of old Asturias, from Oviedo, go to Liyūn; the four of Cantabria, from Santander, to Burghush; the ten of the Basque coast, from Bilbao, to Banbalūna

data.note: made after the save of 3 November and before that of 5 November; the Galician ṭāʾifa's records date it to 3 November

title: The other 23 towns of Galicia, from Santiago, A Coruña and Lugo to Ourense and Tui, are made a ṭāʾifa of the Emperor under Diego Sotomaior, a Galician noble of the faith, thirty-one years old. The empire now has eight ṭāʾifas
